name: Intel Arc B580
memory_bandwidth_basis: Intel ARK spec table: 'Graphics Memory Bandwidth 456 GB/s' together with 'Graphics Memory Speed 19 Gbps' and 'Graphics Memory Interface 192 bit' (19 Gbps x 192-bit / 8 = 456 GB/s, consistent)
notes:
Consumer Battlemage part: 20 Xe-cores, 160 Xe Matrix Extensions (XMX) engines, 20 RT units, 2670 MHz graphics clock, TSMC N5, PCIe 4.0 x8 (note x8, NOT x16), 190 W TBP, device ID 0xE20B, $249 RCP, launched Q4'24.

PRECISION CAVEAT - and Intel's labelling is better than NVIDIA's: the only throughput figure in the ARK table is 'GPU Peak TOPS (Int8) 233'. Intel's own Arc Pro B60 datasheet defines the equivalent figure as 'the peak throughput when running XMX workloads with INT8 datatype and DENSE models'. So 233 TOPS should be read as DENSE INT8 - an integer matmul figure, NOT an FP16 number and NOT an INT4 number. No FP16/BF16/FP8 throughput is published for this part in ARK, so none is recorded here.

Inference: 12 GB at 456 GB/s. Capacity is the binding constraint by a wide margin. Also note the x8 PCIe interface: half the Gen4 x16 link rate matters for weight streaming from system RAM and for multi-GPU host transfers, which is a real penalty for offload-based workflows.
